instruction: Please implement a Q&A website that answers user-submitted questions. The website should have functionalities for submitting questions, answering questions, and viewing answers. Users should be able to submit questions, view answers, and rate the answers. Set overall background to beige, then style components with saddle brown.

ui_instruct.task: Submit a new question using the question submission form.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The question is successfully posted and appears on the list of submitted questions.

ui_instruct.task: View the list of submitted questions.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A list of submitted questions is displayed, including the latest question, sorted appropriately.

ui_instruct.task: Submit an answer to an existing question.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The answer is successfully posted and visible under the corresponding question.

ui_instruct.task: View answers to a specific question.
ui_instruct.expected_result: All answers related to the specific question are displayed clearly beneath the question.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'beige' as the background color and 'saddle brown' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'beige' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'saddle brown', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The homepage list needs to become a real browse experience. Clear out any demo questions and seed exactly these seven, I'll add more later: 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' (#cooking, +8, 3 answers), 'Best budget airlines in Europe?' (#travel, +5, 2 answers), 'Why is my laptop fan always loud?' (#tech, +5, 4 answers), 'Is intermittent fasting safe for beginners?' (#fitness, +12, 1 answer), 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?' (#fitness, 0, no answers yet), 'What's the best way to learn Python?' (#tech, +8, no answers yet), and 'Can I freeze fresh basil?' (#cooking, -2, 1 answer). Above the list give me toggleable tag pills (picking several means a question matching any of them counts), an answered/unanswered choice that combines with the tags, a 'Showing X of Y questions' readout that never lies, and sorting by score, highest first — when two questions tie on score, the one with more answers takes the higher spot. Two style things I want everywhere in this app, now and for anything we build later: scores always wear their sign (+8, -2, a bare 0 only for zero), and tags always render as lowercase pills with a # up front.
follow_ups.source_feature: Tag-Based Filtering (fused with Quora's topic/category organization)

ui_instruct.task: Open the question list with no filters applied and read the questions from top to bottom.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Order is: intermittent fasting (+12), sourdough starter (+8), learn Python (+8), laptop fan (+5), budget airlines (+5), bike wheel (0), freeze basil (-2). In particular the laptop fan question (4 answers) sits above budget airlines (2 answers) despite both being +5, and sourdough (3 answers) sits above Python (0 answers).

ui_instruct.task: Toggle on the #tech and #fitness tag pills and select the unanswered option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two questions show — 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?' and 'What's the best way to learn Python?' — and the readout says Showing 2 of 7 questions.

ui_instruct.task: Toggle on the #cooking tag pill and select the unanswered option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: No questions match, and a sensible empty-state message appears instead of a blank area, leftover rows, or a crash.

ui_instruct.task: Open 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?', post an answer using the answering form, then go back to the question list and select the unanswered option with no tag pills active.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Only 'What's the best way to learn Python?' remains in the unanswered view — the bike wheel question no longer qualifies as unanswered.

ui_instruct.task: Open the question 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' and look at its answers.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Three answers are listed under the question.

follow_ups.instruction: Rework the ask form into a proper composer. As I type the title, show live suggestions of existing questions whose titles contain what I've typed — ignore case, don't start suggesting until I've typed at least 3 characters, and show each match with its tag pill and its score. Enforce while I type, not just on submit: title between 15 and 120 characters with a live character counter, it has to end with a question mark, exactly one tag picked, and the post button stays locked with a clear reason until everything's right. One more thing for the whole app going forward: any question with zero answers gets a small amber 'Needs answer' badge wherever it shows up.

ui_instruct.task: Open the ask composer and type how into the title field.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two duplicate suggestions appear: 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' and 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?'.

ui_instruct.task: In the composer, type the title Why is it hot? into the title field.
ui_instruct.expected_result: While typing, a message about the minimum title length (it's only 14 characters, under the 15 minimum) appears and the post control stays locked.

ui_instruct.task: Clear the title field, type ho, then add one more letter to make it how.
ui_instruct.expected_result: At two characters no suggestions show; the moment the third character lands the suggestion list appears — it reacts per keystroke, not only on submit.

ui_instruct.task: Type basil into the composer's title field and look at the suggestion that appears.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The single suggestion for 'Can I freeze fresh basil?' shows its tag as a lowercase #cooking pill and its score with the minus sign visible as -2, matching the app-wide signed-score and tag-pill styles.

ui_instruct.task: Toggle on the #tech and #fitness tag pills and select the unanswered option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two questions show — 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?' and 'What's the best way to learn Python?' — and the readout says Showing 2 of 7 questions.

follow_ups.instruction: Time to crown answers. On a question's page, order the answers by rating, best first, and put an Accept control on each so the asker can mark the one that solved it — the accepted answer gets a green checkmark badge and pins to the very top regardless of its rating, and only one answer can hold it at a time (accepting another moves the check over). Once a question has an accepted answer it reads as Solved with a green badge back on the main list too, and the screener gets a Solved option alongside answered/unanswered. Start with the top-rated answer on the sourdough question already accepted.

ui_instruct.task: Open 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?'.
ui_instruct.expected_result: One answer carries a green accepted checkmark badge and is pinned at the very top of the answer list.

ui_instruct.task: On the sourdough question's page, click Accept on a different answer than the currently accepted one.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The accepted checkmark moves to the newly accepted answer, which is now pinned to the top; exactly one answer is accepted and the previous one has lost its badge.

ui_instruct.task: In the question list's screener, select the Solved option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly one question shows: 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' — not the five questions that merely have answers.

ui_instruct.task: Open 'Can I freeze fresh basil?', click Accept on its answer, then go back to the question list and select the Solved option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Two questions now show — sourdough and basil — and the basil question carries the green Solved badge in the list.

ui_instruct.task: Open the question list with no filters applied and read the questions from top to bottom.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Order is: intermittent fasting (+12), sourdough starter (+8), learn Python (+8), laptop fan (+5), budget airlines (+5), bike wheel (0), freeze basil (-2). In particular the laptop fan question (4 answers) sits above budget airlines (2 answers) despite both being +5, and sourdough (3 answers) sits above Python (0 answers).

follow_ups.instruction: Tags deserve their own home — give me a Topics page with a card per tag showing its question count, its combined score across those questions (signed like everywhere else — cooking should land at +6 from the +8 sourdough and the -2 basil), how many of its questions are solved (got an accepted answer), and the tag's top question by score. Order the cards by question count, biggest first, and go alphabetical when counts tie.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Topics page and read the tag cards in order.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Cards read #cooking, #fitness, #tech, #travel — the three two-question tags alphabetical ahead of #travel with 1 — and NOT ordered by combined score (which would put #tech, at +13, first).

ui_instruct.task: Open the Topics page and count the tag cards.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly four cards, one per tag — no tag duplicated even though most tags have multiple questions, and none missing; the page renders without crashing.

ui_instruct.task: Look at the #cooking card on the Topics page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: It shows 2 questions, a combined score of +6 with the plus sign visible, 1 solved, and its top question is 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?'.

ui_instruct.task: Open 'Can I freeze fresh basil?', click Accept on its answer, then open the Topics page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The #cooking card's solved count now reads 2 — both cooking questions are solved.

ui_instruct.task: Open the ask composer and type how into the title field.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two duplicate suggestions appear: 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' and 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?'.

follow_ups.instruction: Let's add bounties to drum up answers. Each question gets a bounty tool: I type a point amount and a live panel shows my remaining balance updating as I type — I start with 500 points, the amount has to be at least 50, in steps of 25, and within what's left, and the confirm stays locked with the reason shown the instant the number's off. Featured (bountied) questions get their own Featured strip pinned above the main list, biggest bounty first with each bounty shown, and the strip stays put no matter what filters are switched on below it. Kick things off with 75 points already sitting on the bike wheel question, so I'm down to 425.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bounty tool on 'What's the best way to learn Python?' and type 49, then change it to 60, then to 75.
ui_instruct.expected_result: At 49 an under-the-50-minimum message shows and confirm is locked; at 60 it stays locked because 60 isn't a step of 25; at 75 the error clears and confirm unlocks — each reaction happening as the value is typed.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bounty tool on 'What's the best way to learn Python?' and type 50.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The balance starts at 425 (500 minus the 75 already on the bike wheel), and as soon as 50 is typed the live remaining preview reads 375.

ui_instruct.task: In the bounty tool on 'What's the best way to learn Python?', type 100 and confirm it.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Featured strip now lists the Python question (100 pts) above the bike wheel question (75 pts) — biggest bounty first — with each entry showing its bounty.

ui_instruct.task: In the screener, toggle on the #travel tag pill.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The main list narrows to just 'Best budget airlines in Europe?' while the Featured strip above it still shows the bike wheel question with its 75-pt bounty.

ui_instruct.task: Toggle on the #cooking tag pill and select the unanswered option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: No questions match, and a sensible empty-state message appears instead of a blank area, leftover rows, or a crash.

follow_ups.instruction: People keep spotting typos in answers, so: put a Suggest Edit control on every answer that opens the current text ready for revising, with submissions landing on a new Review page — and give its nav link a pending-count badge. Each pending entry shows the question's title and its tag, the original and proposed text side by side, and Approve/Reject: approving swaps the new text in on the question page with an 'edited' marker, rejecting changes nothing — either way the entry leaves the queue and the badge count drops. Seed one pending suggestion already sitting there, a wording fix on the basil question's answer, and when the queue's empty say so warmly instead of showing a bare page.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Review page from the navigation.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The nav link carries a pending badge reading 1, and the single queue entry is the seeded suggestion on the basil question's answer, showing original and proposed text side by side with Approve and Reject controls.

ui_instruct.task: On the Review page click Approve on the basil suggestion, then open 'Can I freeze fresh basil?'.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The queue now shows its friendly empty message with the pending badge at zero or gone, and the basil answer displays the proposed text with an 'edited' marker.

ui_instruct.task: On the Review page click Reject on the basil suggestion, then open 'Can I freeze fresh basil?'.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The entry leaves the queue, and the basil answer still shows its original text with no 'edited' marker.

ui_instruct.task: Look at the basil entry on the Review page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Its question's tag appears as a lowercase #cooking pill, matching the app-wide tag style.

ui_instruct.task: In the question list's screener, select the Solved option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly one question shows: 'How do I keep sourdough starter alive?' — not the five questions that merely have answers.

follow_ups.instruction: I want a follow-and-digest setup. Put a Follow toggle on every question, and build a Digest page that assembles a plain-text roundup right on screen with a copy control: first line 'Following N questions', then one line per followed question — title, tag, signed score, answer count — ordered by score, highest first, with a 'FEATURED — 75 pts'-style tag tacked onto the end of any line whose question carries a bounty. Start me off already following the bike wheel question and then the sourdough one, let me unfollow straight from the Digest page with the text redoing itself instantly, and when I'm following nothing show a friendly nothing-to-build note instead of an empty box.
follow_ups.source_feature: Follow a Question (extended into an on-screen digest builder)

ui_instruct.expected_result: The first line says Following 2 questions, and the sourdough line (+8) sits above the bike wheel line (0) — score order, not the order they were followed in (bike wheel was followed first).

ui_instruct.task: Find the bike wheel question's line in the digest text.
ui_instruct.expected_result: It shows the #fitness tag, its score as a bare 0 with no sign, 0 answers, and ends with a FEATURED marker carrying 75 pts — while the sourdough line carries no featured marker.

ui_instruct.task: On the Digest page, unfollow both followed questions.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The digest text is replaced immediately by the friendly nothing-to-build message — no stale lines, no blank panel, no crash.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bounty tool on the sourdough question, type 100, confirm it, then open the Digest page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The sourdough line now ends with a 100-pt FEATURED marker while keeping its spot above the bike wheel line.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Topics page and read the tag cards in order.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Cards read #cooking, #fitness, #tech, #travel — the three two-question tags alphabetical ahead of #travel with 1 — and NOT ordered by combined score (which would put #tech, at +13, first).

follow_ups.instruction: Time to tighten the look everywhere it applies — the question list with its screener, the Topics page, the Review page, and the Digest page, all four the same: keep the beige background, but every primary action button becomes saddle brown with white text and pill-shaped fully rounded corners; page titles sit centered at the top of each page; every card or list entry gets a 1px saddle-brown border with a 12px corner radius; the green Solved and accepted badges become dark green pills with white text; and section headings render in small caps. Don't let a single one of those pages drift from the rest.
follow_ups.source_feature: Consistent badge/pill design language across pages (adapted as a site-wide restyle)

ui_instruct.expected_result: At 49 an under-the-50-minimum message shows and confirm is locked; at 60 it stays locked because 60 isn't a step of 25; at 75 the error clears and confirm unlocks — each reaction happening as the value is typed.

follow_ups.instruction: The capstone: a Triage dashboard I can run the whole site from. Up top, a headline row with how many questions are still open (no accepted answer yet), how many are solved, and how many edit suggestions await review. Below that, two ranked sections: unanswered questions by urgency — bigger bounty first, then score, then A-Z on the title — each row showing tag, score, and its bounty if it has one; and answered-but-not-solved (has answers, nothing accepted) by score, with ties going to the question with more answers, same as the main list does it. Solved questions stay out of both sections.
follow_ups.source_feature: Bounty / Reward System (fused with review-queue moderation into a triage dashboard)

ui_instruct.expected_result: 'How to fix a wobbly bike wheel?' (75-pt bounty, score 0) ranks ABOVE 'What's the best way to learn Python?' (+8, no bounty) — bounty outranks score.

ui_instruct.expected_result: Order is: intermittent fasting (+12), laptop fan (+5, 4 answers), budget airlines (+5, 2 answers), freeze basil (-2) — laptop above airlines on the answer-count tiebreak, and sourdough absent because it's solved.

ui_instruct.task: Open 'Is intermittent fasting safe for beginners?', click Accept on its answer, then return to the Triage dashboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The fasting question has left the answered-but-not-solved section, and the solved total in the headline row now reads 2.

ui_instruct.task: On the Review page click Approve on the basil suggestion, then open the Triage dashboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The pending edit suggestions count in the headline row reads 0, down from 1.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Digest page and read the generated text.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The first line says Following 2 questions, and the sourdough line (+8) sits above the bike wheel line (0) — score order, not the order they were followed in (bike wheel was followed first).

target_app_summary: The base beige-and-saddle-brown Q&A site grows into a full community knowledge platform. A pinned seven-question seed powers a tag screener with boolean tag/status filtering and tie-aware score sorting; an ask composer adds live duplicate detection and strict validation; an accept-answer workflow introduces a Solved state that propagates into the screener, a Topics analytics hub, and a capstone Triage dashboard. A points-based bounty system feeds a Featured strip, the follow-and-digest builder, and the Triage urgency ranking, while an edit-suggestion review queue adds moderation whose pending count also lands on Triage. A site-wide restyle pass locks visual consistency across the screener, Topics, Review, and Digest pages. The graph runs several chains three-plus deep (base list -> screener -> bounties -> triage; base answers -> accept workflow -> topics/triage), so early breakage compounds.

global_rules.rule: Scores always display with an explicit sign everywhere in the app: +8, -2, and a bare 0 only for zero.
Tags always render as lowercase pills prefixed with # everywhere they appear.
Any question with zero answers shows a small amber 'Needs answer' badge wherever it is listed, on all current and future surfaces.

pinned_seed.entity: 7 seeded questions with tags, signed scores, and answer counts
pinned_seed.records_gist: sourdough #cooking +8/3ans; airlines #travel +5/2ans; laptop fan #tech +5/4ans; fasting #fitness +12/1ans; bike wheel #fitness 0/0ans; python #tech +8/0ans; basil #cooking -2/1ans
